Subject: CloudSphere private offer — SKU entitlements & reseller surcharge question

Hi Sergio / Irene,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. We're getting our procurement and channel ops teams aligned before we submit the private offer for Marketplace listing. Two quick questions that came up and wanted Redwood's input before we lock the numbers: 

1) SKU entitlements: we want to include a small ancillary SKU that represents our managed onboarding/ops support (monthly). Is it better to list that as a separate SKU on the private offer or bundle it into the compute SKU as an "add-on"? We prefer separate SKUs for accounting clarity, but I know some marketplaces prefer simplicity.

2) Reseller surcharge / pass-through: our reseller partners expect a surcharge on top of list price (for handling billing/regulatory compliance). They asked for a 12% reseller surcharge. Is that something Redwood can support as an explicit pass-through line in the private offer, or would you recommend Redwood invoice the consolidated amount and pay partners out-of-band?

I've attached an early draft of the pricing spreadsheet and a proposed term sheet so you have context.

Appreciate any guidance — we're aiming to submit the PO by next Wednesday.

Best,

Elaine — thanks for the attachments, got them. High level thoughts below; I'll loop in Billing/Marketplace and Product for the edge cases but wanted to give a quick path forward so you can keep procurement moving.

On SKU entitlements:
- Separate SKU: easiest for CloudSphere orgs (accounting + usage tracking). Redwood supports multi-SKU private offers, so listing a small "Managed Onboarding" SKU is fine.
- Bundle: simpler UX for end-customers and simplifies marketplace presentation, but makes partner settlement a bit messier.

On reseller surcharge / pass-through:
- We generally recommend explicit pass-through lines if partners need to see their margin clearly. That is, the private offer lists base SKU prices and a separate line for "Partner Reseller Surcharge (pass-through)". This keeps invoicing transparent.
- Caveat: some marketplaces (esp. older regions) don't allow arbitrary surcharge lines on the main listing and ask that any reseller fees be handled off-marketplace. We should confirm for AWS/GCP/Azure specific to the regional marketplace you're targeting.

If CloudSphere is pushing a 12% surcharge, two options we see:
A) Marketplace-visible pass-through (preferred for transparency): Redwood lists an explicit surcharge SKU with zero usage caps; Redwood invoices consolidated amount and marks the surcharge as pass-through so partner payouts are automated. Needs marketplace approval.
B) Off-marketplace settlement: set list prices to be net of partner fees and CloudSphere invoices partner separately. Cleaner from marketplace compliance standpoint but reduces visibility for customers and can complicate revenue recognition.

Next steps from our side: I'll confirm marketplace constraints with Marketplace Ops (we support both AWS/GCP/Azure but rules differ). Can you confirm expected monthly committed usage, and whether partners need surcharge applied per invoice or as a monthly settlement? That will determine routing.

Thanks — will follow up with a short ops note once we confirm platform constraints.

— Sergio Alvarez
Head of Channel Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Folks — forwarding the ask from CloudSphere. Key points for ops/legal review:

- CloudSphere wants a distinct managed-onboarding SKU + explicit partner surcharge at ~12% that must appear on-customer-invoice (per their partners' ask).
- Committed volume ~ $1.1M Y1; partner surcharge applied per invoice.
- They prefer marketplace-visible pass-through.

Options to consider (summary for decision):
1) Approve explicit surcharge SKU as pass-through and enable partner payout automation. Pros: transparency, meets partner expectations. Cons: some marketplaces have listing restrictions and we may need marketplace approval cycles per region. Implication for billing: mark surcharge as passthrough revenue (no revenue recognition until settlement).
2) Require CloudSphere to absorb partner surcharge and raise list prices so Redwood invoices a single consolidated number. Pros: avoids marketplace listing friction. Cons: reduces partner transparency and may complicate CloudSphere's partner margins.

Action items:
- Ben: can you confirm revenue recognition/tax implications if we label surcharge as pass-through vs embedded?
- Irene: can you quick-check AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace rules on extra fee lines for private offers (region-specific)?
- Marissa: if we go with surcharge as an explicit SKU, what's the recommended wording and tiering for a 12% partner surcharge so it's consistent with our existing private-offer language?

I'll draft a follow-up note to send to CloudSphere once we have your inputs.

— Sergio

Sergio — quick take from Finance/Billing:

- Pass-through labeling: doable, but treat it as non-revenue (contra/clearing) until partner settlement is confirmed. That means we can't recognize the 12% as software revenue on our P&L; it will flow through a clearing account. Need CloudSphere's partner agreement (legal) confirming settlement mechanics.
- Tax/VAT: if the surcharge is separately itemized and passed through, it may trigger different VAT handling in EU/UK — flagging in case CloudSphere expands regionally.
- Recommendation: allow explicit surcharge SKU, but cap internal processing to: 1) single-line surcharge per invoice; 2) automated partner payout via our partner settlement pipeline. This limits custom work and is consistent with existing partner flows.

I'll draft suggested wording for the private offer entry:
"Partner Reseller Handling Fee (pass-through) — X% of list price; billed on each invoice and remitted to partner per settlement schedule."

If you want, I can send a 1-page ops note and a sample private-offer JSON that includes the surcharge SKU and settlement mapping by Monday.

— Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
